 Ticket prices for Kentucky's game against Grambling State are a bad sign
 Adam Stratton @ AdamStrattonKSR 21h 6 Share Share 
 Regardless of the year, Kentucky basketball played inside Rupp Arena is always the hottest ticket in Lexington. Getting to watch the winningest program in history play in one of the greatest venues in college sports is a privilege, and usually one that requires a decent investment from the checking account. With Mark Pope’s squad flailing, however, that has changed, and it speaks to the psyche of the Big Blue Nation.
 As of the time of this writing on Sunday afternoon, you can buy a ticket on StubHub to watch Kentucky play a men’s basketball game inside Rupp Arena for $6. Six. Freaking. Dollars. You can’t even buy a soft-serve ice cream cone for $6. Granted, that $6 seat is in the nosebleeds alongside the lowly media, but if you really want to splurge, you can spend $14 for a lower-level seat. Ticket holders are offloading their seats by the truckload, trying to salvage what few dollars they can get back.
 Sure, the opponent is Grambling State, but Big Blue Nation has never let the fact that the ‘Cats are playing a school they’ve never heard of stop them from showing up. That appears to no longer true.
 The word ‘apathy’ gets thrown around a lot as the marker of the downfall of a program. Once fans lose interest, everything spirals out of control quickly. While some fans have certainly voiced their desire to do anything else in their life, including sleep, rather than watch the entirety of the Kentucky basketball game in 2026, that sentiment seems to come from depression, not apathy. It is as if they are resigned to defeat instead of not caring about the outcome of the game.
 That mentality has now shown itself through the secondary ticket market. $6 to get in? $14 for a lower-level seat? It is hard to fathom fans actively avoiding watching Kentucky basketball to this degree, but that is what a 20-point loss to Kansas, a one-point victory (that should have never happened) over Northern Arizona, and a limited prospect of improvement will do. Hope, it seems, has all but dissipated. 
 Kentucky Athletics measures attendance by tickets sold, not by the number of people actually in the building, so their official figure on Monday night will be higher than reality. COVID may long be over, but it may look like everyone is practicing social distancing again. It begs the question: if an embarrassing loss happens and no one is in the arena to see it, does it still count?
 Let’s not find out. The only way out of this BBN dejection plague is to win and keep winning. Until then, take a look in your couch cushions for loose change. It will likely get you inside Rupp Arena.
